title: The impact of generative artificial intelligence on socioeconomic inequalities and policy making

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewing empirical literature and proposing future experimental designs to assess AI's impact on wage inequality, labor displacement, and the digital divide across varying educational and resource backgrounds in work, education, and healthcare.

Reviewing existing studies on automated translation stereotypes (e.g., associating 'nurse' with females and 'doctor' with males) and the reduction of demographic bias in AI-assisted clinical triage decisions.

Evaluating existing literature on biased healthcare algorithms, including diagnostic criteria (e.g., knee X-rays) and cost-based medical resource allocation that disparately impacts underserved and marginalized populations.

Theoretical evaluation of the limitations of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) and convenience sampling in aligning AI with globally and culturally diverse human values and moral preferences.
Reviewing behavioral game theory research demonstrating that large language models systematically overestimate human altruism and underestimate self-interest and inequity-aversion.
